Renewable Thermal Collaborative (2022). Electric Heat Pumps: Renewable Thermal Technology (technology perspective brief, analysis by Boston Consulting Group). 11 slides. https://www.renewablethermal.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/RTC-Vision-Heat-Pumps-FINAL.pdf. No date printed: year from the PDF creation date (10 Nov 2022) and May 2022 price data; to-get.csv cites it as September 2023.

Locators are PDF page (slide) numbers; slides are unnumbered. This brief is the same slide set as the Electric Heat Pumps technology perspective in rtc_2023_001 (its pp.131-140; the COP/LCOH matrix is identical on its p.136). To avoid double counting, numbers already extracted under rtc_2023_001 are NOT repeated here: dairy (COP 4.2, 10-88 degC) and lumber (COP 3-4.6, reprinted from Minea 2012) case studies on p.5, conservative COP 3 and gas efficiency 85% (pp.7-9). New here: the COP and LCOH matrix by source and output temperature (p.6) - 222 cells, in full in _cop-lcoh-matrix.csv (not loaded; columns input and output temperature, lift, COP, LCOH 2022 USD/MMBtu; output columns assigned by the rule that each row starts at max(50, source+5) degC and runs in 5 K steps, checked against the layout), with six illustrative cells in the main file (source 50 degC at 20/40/60 K lift, 30->80, 80->120, 90->160); the payback-analysis capex assumption of 120,000 USD/MMBtu (ACEEE); temperature limit and maturity. Not extracted: state bar charts (pp.7-8) and emissions maps (p.9).
(1) Capex unit printed as $/MMBtu, presumably $/(MMBtu/h). (2) p.3 heading says "Key properties of solar thermal heating" on the heat pump slide (copy error). (3) No date printed.
